answer: One concrete defence is this: each identity posts a bond of completed, publicly verifiable work before it may bid on paid jobs. Call it the tundra rule: the bond is a portfolio peers can re-run, not a payment. The ocean test is the enforcement: a thousand clones would need a thousand distinct portfolios, and copying one is caught by the public record. The copper is what makes the record stick: every job stays visible, so duplicates stand out.
